content:
Kevin Osei: putting up `modules/security-groups-baseline` for Private VPC alpha. Need security eyes on defaults before we merge. PR is up and I’m trying to keep it “secure-by-default” but not block weird enterprise networks.

Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-terraform/pull/246

Main questions:
1) Do we default egress to `0.0.0.0/0` (Terraform AWS SG default) or force explicit egress rules?
2) Do we include NACLs in alpha modules (opinionated) or just document recommended NACLs?
3) Any must-have ports to lock down / tighten for installer + control plane?

Marcus Lin: :eyes: taking a look. quick gut: don’t ship wide-open egress by default.

Marcus Lin: ok read through.

High-level: SG set looks reasonable but we need to tighten the defaults and add explicit “escape hatches” as inputs.

Checklist I’m reviewing against (alpha, but still):
- No public ingress by default (0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0)
- Default deny inbound except from known peer SGs / VPC CIDR (where needed)
- No SSH/RDP
- Egress should be explicit and explainable; allow-all egress must be an opt-in with scary docs
- Private-only mode should not require NAT
- If private endpoints are enabled, restrict egress to endpoint SGs and/or VPC prefix lists where possible
- Avoid “self-referencing SG everywhere” patterns that make future auditing impossible
- Inputs validated (port ranges, CIDRs)

Requested changes:
1) Right now `aws_security_group.*` resources include the AWS provider’s implicit `egress all` unless we define egress blocks. Please define explicit egress rules for the components we manage. Add var `allow_all_egress` default `false` and when `true` explicitly create `0.0.0.0/0` egress.
2) For intra-component comms, prefer referencing SG IDs (source_security_group_id) rather than VPC CIDR. Some rules currently allow `var.vpc_cidr` to reach internal ports; that’s too broad in shared VPCs.
3) Control plane -> nodes: confirm exact ports. I see 443/8443 used inconsistently. If we don’t know, at least avoid adding 0-65535 “within VPC” rules.
4) Add notes in README about DNS: if instances need to hit resolver, they’ll need UDP/TCP 53 egress to the VPC resolver, but SG rules might not be needed depending on where this runs (EKS pods vs EC2). Clarify what layer this module targets.

On NACLs: please do NOT create opinionated NACLs in alpha. Too easy to brick installs + customer environments vary (TGW, centralized egress, inspection). But do include guidance + a “known-good” template in docs.

Kevin Osei: super helpful. on (2) SG references: we can do that for our SG-to-SG rules, but for “existing VPC adoption mode” we might not have all SG IDs from customer side. For those I used vpc CIDR as a fallback.

Marcus Lin: fallback is ok but make it explicit and disabled by default.

Suggestion: `allow_vpc_cidr_ingress = false` default. If true, allow from `var.vpc_cidr` on a small set of ports (and document it’s for shared networking / customer-managed SGs).

Irene Choi: +1 on not baking NACLs into terraform modules. customers already have NACLs, TGW, AWS Network Firewall, etc. We’ll spend all our time debugging “why is kube-dns broken” and it’ll be some NACL deny.

Victor Alvarez: agree. NACLs are also stateless, so we’d need symmetric rules (ephemeral ports, etc). We can provide a reference table (ingress/egress + ephemeral range) but don’t enforce.

Hanae Suzuki: on egress: for “private-only endpoints/no NAT” scenario, we should make sure the egress rules don’t *accidentally* require internet. i.e. avoid forcing `0.0.0.0/0:443` as the default.

Also consider KMS / Secrets Manager: do we need those endpoints for Private alpha? If yes, module should at least not prevent them (either optional interface endpoints + egress to them, or document requirement).

Ethan Park: installer side: we’ve seen failures when STS isn’t reachable (role assumption + token calls). In private-only environments, that’s via Interface endpoint for STS.

If SG baseline is going to restrict egress, we need to ensure:
- egress 443 to STS endpoint ENIs (if used)
- egress 443 to ECR API/DKR endpoints
- egress 443 to CloudWatch Logs endpoint (if shipping logs)

S3 is gateway endpoint so SG doesn’t apply there (but route tables do).

Benji Okafor: +1. Also installer does DNS checks; if we restrict egress too far and they use a custom resolver, they’ll get confusing errors. If we can, add outputs / docs indicating “these SGs assume VPC-provided DNS resolver” and how to override.

Kevin Osei: ok.

Current module creates SGs for:
- `redwood_control_plane_sg`
- `redwood_worker_sg`
- `redwood_observability_sg` (for log shipper / metrics sidecars)

Right now I did:
- ingress: mostly SG-to-SG and a couple `vpc_cidr` rules
- egress: none defined (so provider default allow-all)

I’ll change to explicit egress.

Bruno Silva: from PS side, default deny egress is good but we need a clean way to add “customer approved egress” (proxy, firewall, NAT). Suggest you expose `extra_egress_rules` as a list input with validation (ports + cidrs + description). Most customers want to route through inspection but still need some things.

Marcus Lin: careful with `extra_egress_rules` list — terraform type ends up as complex object; but doable. Make sure docs say “use sparingly.”

But for alpha: simplest is fine:
- `allow_all_egress` (default false)
- `allowed_egress_cidrs` + `allowed_egress_ports` maybe
- and “known endpoints mode” where you pass in endpoint SG ids and we allow 443 to those.

Kevin Osei: makes sense. I can do `endpoint_security_group_ids` input and then create egress to those SGs on 443.

Question: should we restrict intra-SG traffic? e.g. worker->worker for clustering. Right now `self = true` for a couple rules.

Victor Alvarez: for k8s nodes, self-referencing SG can be necessary (node-to-node). But scope it to required ports only. Don’t do “all traffic” self.

Marcus Lin: exactly. If you need node-to-node, pin ports (kubelet, overlay, etc) OR treat it as “installer-managed cluster SGs” and keep our module focused on Redwood app components. If we don’t know the k8s ports confidently, don’t guess.

Ethan Park: Redwood installer currently assumes it’s given:
- subnet IDs
- endpoint IDs
- SG IDs for Redwood components

It does not create EKS SG rules. So keep SG module scoped to Redwood workloads; leave EKS cluster/node SGs to customer or separate module.

Hanae Suzuki: +1 scope discipline. If we start mixing k8s infra SGs + Redwood SGs in one baseline, we’ll never make everyone happy.

Kevin Osei: ok, scoping SG baseline to Redwood components only.

Proposed changes I’ll make:
- Define explicit egress blocks (no implicit allow-all).
- Add `allow_all_egress` (default false).
- Add `endpoint_security_group_ids` and allow TCP/443 egress to those SGs.
- Remove/disable `vpc_cidr` ingress fallback by default; add `allow_vpc_cidr_ingress` (default false) for shared VPC adopters.
- Tighten any `self = true` rules to only ports we actually need (or remove if not needed).
- Add README section: “NACLs: not managed by this module; guidance only” + link to forthcoming Confluence page.

Marcus Lin: that addresses my security concerns for alpha.

One more nit: please add variable validation for port lists (1-65535) and CIDR format. And add a small table in README:
- which component
- direction
- port
- source/destination
- why needed

That helps security reviewers at customers.

Irene Choi: re NACL guidance: include a warning about ephemeral ports and statefulness. We’ve been burned by “deny all high ports” NACLs. If we publish a template, it needs to be correct or we’ll create incidents.

Victor Alvarez: I can send you a reference snippet for the NACL template text (not terraform resource), just recommended rules with comments.

Kevin Osei: awesome. I’ll implement and ping for re-review.

Marcus Lin: :thumbsup: once updates are in, tag me and Kevin (Osei) for final pass. If we ship with explicit egress + NACL guidance only, I’m comfortable signing off for alpha.

(Reaction: :thumbsup: from Hanae Suzuki)
(Reaction: :thumbsup: from Irene Choi)

Kevin Osei: pushed commits w/ explicit egress + new vars. Also updated README with the table. Re-review when you have a sec.

Marcus Lin: reviewed latest diff. Looks good. Only change requested: rename `allow_vpc_cidr_ingress` -> `enable_vpc_cidr_ingress_fallback` (makes it harder to misunderstand).

Kevin Osei: done.

Marcus Lin: approved. Security sign-off for SG defaults (alpha) assuming NACL doc ships as guidance and we keep “allow all egress” opt-in.

Ethan Park: thanks all — this will also make installer preflight errors way more actionable when endpoints are missing.

Benji Okafor: +1, and README table is going to save us in customer security reviews.
